# 5 reasons you need a Garmin inReach


November 12, 2026


By Garmin team


### *When the adventure calls, bring your Garmin inReach along for the ride.*


Exploring the great outdoors can be exhilarating, mysterious and rewarding.


But even the most beautiful places on Earth can turn dangerous in an instant.


Here are several reasons to bring a Garmin inReach® satellite communicator1 on your next adventure.


## 1. Trust


When building your outdoor kit, there is no room for gear that doesn’t perform when it matters most. Over time, you whittle down the products in your pack to those you know you can depend on. In short, you take the products you can trust.


That trust is why[Garmin inReach devices](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/c/outdoor-recreation/satellite-communicators/) are used by outdoor enthusiasts and adventurers globally, whether on land, air or sea. This trust has been earned through countless hours of real-world use in remote environments where reliable communication can make a difference.


As a witness to this trust, Garmin inReach has supported over 20,000 SOS incidents, thanks to its two-way communication and SOS functionality.


[Learn who uses inReach devices and why SOS incidents are declared](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/blog/outdoor/2025-inreach-sos-year-in-review/) .


## 2. Purpose-built


For those who venture beyond cellular coverage, inReach is purpose-built for reliable communication, location sharing and emergency assistance in remote environments.


While inReach devices can do many things, every feature is designed with a specific purpose in mind and refined through years of customer feedback and real-world use. Core capabilities include two-way messaging, interactive SOS through Garmin Response℠, tracking, location sharing and the ability to communicate without relying on cellular service.


## 3. Battery life


Emergencies rarely happen when you expect them. Whether you’re heading out for a day hike or a multiday expedition, having an inReach device with you means you’re prepared if plans change. Its long battery life helps ensure it’s ready when you need it most. Here’s a look at battery life specifications for Garmin inReach handhelds:


- [inReach® Mini 3](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/p/1756582/) : up to 350 hours
- [GPSMAP® H1i Plus](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/p/1263273/) : up to 145 hours
- [inReach® Messenger](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/p/793265) : up to 25 days


## 4. Anytime, two-way communication


Two-way communication is a core feature on all inReach products. Thanks to LTE and satellite connectivity on smartwatches with inReach technology, this communication extends to areas beyond cell service. Send and receive messages, get weather forecasts, and navigate and trigger SOS alerts — even when you are out of cell tower range or radio coverage.


Whether you’re checking in with loved ones or coordinating with fellow adventurers, inReach helps keep you connected 24/7 while exploring remote places. And if the unexpected happens, two-way communication can make a critical difference. In an SOS situation, inReach helps connect you to emergency services when it matters most.


## 5. Garmin Response


Based in Montgomery, Texas, the[24/7 Garmin Response team](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/satellite-communicators/interactive-sos-and-garmin-response/) maintains a global database of local first responders, enabling them to quickly reach out to the most appropriate rescue service or other resources in time-critical situations. Through your account, you can save emergency contacts and add notes that might be helpful for an emergency response, such as a trip itinerary, medical conditions or allergies. In the event of an SOS, Garmin Response will be able to view this information and reach out to your emergency contacts to inform them of your situation. You can count on the Garmin Response staff to use their experience to your advantage — and offer support in multiple languages — if you’re ever in need of emergency assistance.


[Learn what happens when you press an SOS](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vEaF2Atxo-s) .


1Active plan required. Some jurisdictions regulate or prohibit the use of satellite communication devices; it is the responsibility of the user to know and follow all applicable laws.
